title: Cellular small object factorizations in locally presentable categories
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with Hom sets in a fixed universe $\mathcal U$ and all $\mathcal U$-small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Suppose $\mathcal C$ is locally presentable: for some infinite regular cardinal $\lambda\in\mathcal U$, a $\mathcal U$-small set of objects $\mathcal P$ generates every object under $\lambda$-filtered colimits and $\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ preserves those colimits for every $P\in\mathcal P$. Here $\lambda$-filtered means that every diagram with fewer than $\lambda$ morphisms admits a cocone, and regular means that a union of fewer than $\lambda$ sets of size less than $\lambda$ has size less than $\lambda$. Let $I$ be a $\mathcal U$-small set of morphisms. For every $f:X\to Y$ there is a factorization $X\xrightarrow{j}Z\xrightarrow{p}Y$ with $pj=f$, such that $p$ has the right lifting property against $I$ and $j$ is a transfinite composition of pushouts of small coproducts of maps of $I$. Explicitly, there are a $\mathcal U$-small ordinal $\theta$ and objects $Z_\alpha$ for $\alpha\leq\theta$, with $Z_0=X$, $Z_\theta=Z$, and $j$ their composite, continuous at every limit ordinal, such that $Z_\alpha\to Z_{\alpha+1}$ is a pushout of $\coprod_{t\in T_\alpha}i_t$ for a $\mathcal U$-small set $T_\alpha$ and maps $i_t\in I$. Continuity means $Z_\beta=\varinjlim_{\alpha<\beta}Z_\alpha$ at every nonzero limit $\beta\leq\theta$. Right lifting means that for every $i:A\to B$ in $I$ and square $pa=bi$ with $a:A\to Z$, $b:B\to Y$, there is $h:B\to Z$ with $hi=a$ and $ph=b$.

source.place: Generic cellular refinement of the small-object input for proof paragraph 2. WANTED: Hovey, Model Categories, Theorem 2.1.14; Adamek and Rosicky, Locally Presentable and Accessible Categories, presentability of every object. Saorin and Stovicek, arXiv:1005.3248v2, Proposition 2.1 (read online, not archived) gives the cellular conclusion under domain smallness. No Stacks tag gives this whole locally-presentable cellular factorization statement.

They do not deduce this hypothesis from local presentability and an arbitrary small set of arrows. OrthogonalReflection concerns a reflection rather than these factorizations.
